meta.title: Hyderabad property-tax payment (current year, residential, known PTIN) grid-only evidence ledger
meta.disclaimer: Independent research, not official advice. Grid-only benchmark run: sources and claims only, no nodes, edges, roadblocks or journeys. Desk research, no counter visited. Limitations: the corporation's only published rate notification covers non-residential buildings and states on its face that there is no revision of property tax on residential buildings, so no reviewed route publishes a rate or amount a residential owner can apply; the payment and receipt routes are public but were read only, with no property tax identification number or mobile number entered and no payment begun; the corporation's Citizen's Charter, which supplies the circle-office structure, states on its face that it was prepared on 10 May 2013 and would be revised on or before 13 May 2014, so claims from it are graded C. Do not submit personal data through this ledger.

scenarios.label: Hyderabad property-tax payment on a known PTIN
scenarios.summary: An individual owner pays the current year's property tax on a residential property already on the municipal register with a known identifier, by the municipal payment route, online portal first and counter or bank route second. First-time assessment, name transfer or mutation, arrears disputes, rebate eligibility beyond what the payment route itself states, and commercial property are excluded.

sources.title: Citizen's Charter - Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation, office structure and property tax section
sources.notes: Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Telangana, India. Agency naming as displayed on the access date: 'Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation'. The document states of itself that it was prepared by the department on 10 May 2013 and would be revised on or before 13 May 2014; the 2013 date is recorded as publishedAt and claims from it are graded C as visibly outdated official material. Archive: an existing Wayback snapshot was found at https://web.archive.org/web/20260420030903/https://ghmc.gov.in/Menu_Files/citizen-charter-19-06_compress.pdf (2026-04-20); no new capture was pushed from this run.

claims.text: The corporation's online payments portal opens property tax payment with a form requiring either a property tax identification number or a registered mobile number, and offers a Know Your PTI Number route beside it.
claims.notes: Matches this scenario's premise of a known property identifier, and gives a second way in for an owner who does not have it.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax page states that there are no manual transactions in tax assessment, issue of special notice, issue of annual demand notices and receipts, and that assessments, notices and collection are fully computerised.
claims.notes: Names an annual demand notice as the instrument by which the liability reaches the owner, without stating when it is issued or when the tax falls due.

claims.text: The corporation's online payments portal publishes a Property Tax Payment Receipts route, reachable without login, that takes a property tax identification number or a registered mobile number, and states that only online paid transactions after 1 April 2016 can be downloaded.
claims.notes: The route's own fields, action and scope notice were observed; nothing was entered, so no claim is made about what it returns.

claims.text: The corporation's published notification on the new system of assessment of property tax fixes the monthly rent per square foot of plinth area for non-residential buildings and states on its face that there is no revision of property tax on residential buildings.
claims.notes: The one rate document the corporation publishes is expressly not about the category this scenario covers.

claims.text: The corporation's published notification states that the procedure for determining annual rental value and assessing property tax is laid down in sections 197 to 238 and 264 to 289 of the Hyderabad Municipal Corporations Act, 1955 and the Hyderabad Municipal Corporations (Assessment of Property Tax) Rules, 1990 as amended, and that it proceeds by dividing the corporation into territorial zones and classifying buildings by construction.
claims.notes: The method is named and its statutory source cited; no residential rate or zone value is given on any reviewed route.

claims.text: The corporation's Citizen's Charter states that the circle office is headed by a Deputy Commissioner and handles all services related to property tax and other municipal taxes and fees.
claims.notes: A designation tied to a jurisdiction rule: the circle in which the property falls. Graded C because the charter is twelve years past the revision date it states for itself.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax page states that property tax can be paid at citizen service centres in all 30 circles and at the corporation head office.
claims.notes: Confirms from a current page the circle structure the charter describes.

claims.text: The corporation's key contacts page gives the head office address at CC Complex Tank Bund Road, Lower Tank Bund, Hyderabad 500063, a helpline number 21111111 and a telephone number 040-23225397, and publishes an officers contacts table with columns for name, designation, contact number and email.
claims.notes: Institutional contact details only. At least one row of the officers table displayed a placeholder rather than a name on the access date.

claims.text: The corporation's online payments portal links published zone and circle maps and circle and ward maps as image files.
claims.notes: A route from a property's location to the circle whose office handles it.

claims.text: The amount of property tax payable on a residential property, and the rate or slab from which it is derived, is not established by any reviewed public page; the corporation's only published rate notification covers non-residential buildings and disclaims any revision for residential ones.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related: the payment route is public and would return the amount, but exercising it requires entering a real property identifier, which is outside the safety boundary.

claims.text: When property tax falls due, and whether any rebate or penalty attaches to paying early or late, is not established by any reviewed public page.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related.

claims.text: What a resident owner must produce to pay property tax on a known identifier is not established by any reviewed public page; the document lists the corporation publishes belong to new assessment and mutation, which this scope excludes.
claims.notes: Retained because the uncertainty itself matters to the journey. Not login-related.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax page states that property tax can be paid through handheld machines of bill collectors integrated with a central server.
claims.notes: One payment channel, split from the compound payment-modes claim at audit. No count attaches to this channel on the page.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax page states that property tax can be paid at 72 Mee-Seva centres within corporation limits.
claims.notes: One payment channel, split from the compound payment-modes claim at audit. The count of 72 is now separately checkable.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax page states that property tax can be paid online or by NEFT and RTGS.
claims.notes: One payment channel, split from the compound payment-modes claim at audit. This is the channel the primary scenario takes first.

claims.text: The corporation's property tax page states that property tax can be paid at 537 branches of 8 banks.
claims.notes: One payment channel, split from the compound payment-modes claim at audit. The counts of 537 and 8 are now separately checkable; the page does not name the banks.
